sections.title: The Lord's Sovereignty and Kingship
observations: This psalm begins with a declaration of the Lord's sovereignty, as He speaks to His anointed one, often interpreted as a reference to the Messiah. The phrase 'Sit at my right hand' signifies a position of power and authority, indicating that the Messiah will reign alongside God.

The imagery of the Lord's enemies being made a footstool emphasizes His ultimate victory over all opposition. This reflects the biblical theme of God's triumph over evil and His establishment of justice.

sections.title: The Priesthood of the Messiah
observations: The psalm introduces the concept of a priest-king, a unique combination that is fulfilled in Christ. The reference to 'a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek' highlights the eternal nature of Christ's priesthood, which is distinct from the Levitical priesthood.
Melchizedek, a figure from Genesis, represents a priesthood that predates and supersedes the Levitical order, suggesting that Christ's priesthood is superior and eternal.

sections.title: The Lord's Judgment and Victory
observations: The psalm concludes with a powerful declaration of the Lord's judgment against the nations. The imagery of the Lord striking down kings and executing judgment reinforces His role as a righteous judge.
This section serves as a reminder of God's ultimate authority over the nations and His ability to bring justice, encouraging believers to trust in His sovereignty.

importantVerses.commentary: The declaration of the Lord's command to the Messiah signifies His exalted status and authority.
The reference to the priesthood of Melchizedek emphasizes the unique and eternal nature of Christ's priesthood.

questions: What does it mean for Christ to be seated at the right hand of God?
How does the priesthood of Melchizedek differ from the Levitical priesthood, and why is this significant?
In what ways does Psalm 110 encourage believers to trust in God's sovereignty and justice?
